A good novel with a story about a lonely student, Koji, and three beautiful girls. You have to choose who to spend the days before Christmas with. I recommend playing this game during the Christmas days.

Sakura Santa is a short romantic visual novel with a seasonal winter theme. The story follows a lonely student during the holidays who encounters supernatural girls. The tone stays cheerful and avoids heavy drama, making it simple to complete in one evening.

Visual presentation is the primary appeal. Character art is bright with consistent quality, and outfits emphasize the holiday aesthetic. Backgrounds capture snowy streets, cozy rooms, and festive settings, adding charm to each scene.

Writing centers on light romantic comedy. Dialogue focuses on friendly interactions rather than deep narrative stakes. The supernatural elements add novelty but do not develop into complex worldbuilding.

Characters fit familiar archetypes. Each route provides mild emotional beats but avoids challenging conflicts. Players seeking comfort and simple romance will find the tone pleasant. Players wanting layered character growth may feel underwhelmed.

Music is soft and repetitive. It supports the cozy mood but lacks memorable tracks. Sound effects are minimal and serve functional roles only.

Player choice exists but does not produce large branching paths. Most decisions lead toward different character endings. Replay value comes from experiencing each route, though differences are modest.

Sakura Santa succeeds as a brief, festive visual novel with cute character art and a gentle holiday theme. It does not offer mechanical depth or ambitious storytelling. Suitable for fans of seasonal romance who want a short, relaxing read.

So yet another Sakura Visual Novel “game” this one with an obviously Christmas theme setting to it.

This Sakura game is actually abit more subdued compared to others, of course there is still cleavage shots but unlike the other games, the stories and yes that is plural, (there is one main theme story here but 4 different endings), isn't about sexualizing the girls (as much) but how/who your going to spend your Christmas.
For some, without Sakura games usual constant hinting at perversion will be abit disappointing for others, it would have probably spoilt the more sweet Christmasy story being told.
And no there isn't any x-rated patch to ‘spice’ this one up. 

It really is more of a sweet, if slightly outrageous story at times begin told here.
In fact, you can keep the story really 'quite' grounded and have a really romantic story if you just focus on one of the girls and her own story ending.
This is the story, though feeling just like one of those straight to TV Christmas films that are out and constantly on during the daytime this time of year that no-one watches, that is probably my preferred story of the different endings, it just fits in with the more ‘sweeter’ tone of this game the best to me.

The other two girls own stories add in a more ‘magical’ ‘unrealistic’ element to events.
With one of them feeling like a character that would best work in a more tradition Sakura game where its, its usual perverted self and the other, know an interesting idea to the mythology of Christmas, kinda feels like apart from that idea, there is nothing else to her character and maybe just added because its Christmas themed.

Sadly, though also with kinda of relief at the same time, the game is still only as long as the other Sakura games, so with three different girls to focus on, the individual story for each girl can feel rather short and lacking, however the depth of writing isn’t exactly enrapturing so doesn't hold my attention as well as good book could, so in that regard, best to play in short bursts, maybe play one story arc, and then play another girls story arc the next day. Either way, I'm glad it didn't just slog on any longer.

So on the whole, I'd probably side thumb this if I could but seeing as how its Christmas I'll give it the benefit of the doubt.
But only get on a sale, as if your looking at this game your probably already familiar with Sakura games and probably enjoy the mix of perverted stories they tell. 
However like I said, this is more sweet that sex, so even if you enjoy focusing more on the story side with this one, once you’ve played it once I doubt you'll ever go back and play it again.

Ive been playing every 'Sakura' title in order of release. This is the 8th released and I think only the second one I've given a positive review too. 

This is a PG rated Sakura game, there is no R18+ content patch for this title.

Writing: They have experimented with comedy in previous titles and in my opinion the combination of innuendo and lewd jokes in this makes it very refreshing and enjoyable to read.

Characters: The characters are actually over 18. Thats been pretty rare so far in the series. Also unlike previous titles there are three heroines and each of them are quite funny. In previous titles there has always been one character whos lines ive found arduous and annoying to read.

Sound: nothing to see here. They are cheap midi files but (unlike previous titles) they dont make you want to drive a pencil into your ear drums.

CG scenes:  Again, its a non-adult title but the CG scenes were much better than the last non-adult Sakura Game I played (Sakura Shrine Girls) which I described the scenes as being "too safe and reserved". Accompanied by the clever writing I quite enjoyed them.

Replay-ability & gameplay:  So this one actually has some semblance of player choice throughout it. The game lets you chose which girl to see each day-to-day, depending on the order you choose different things happen throughout the game unlocking quite a large number of unique scenes. 

Honestly this is far more effort than most of the other Sakura games I've played until this point.. which usually have only short branches or the no real differences based on the choices made.

There are four endings to unlock in total and replaying to get them all is rewarding not because of the CG (which is non-adult) but because of the great writing.
Probably one of the weakest Sakura titles when it comes to writing. Should be considered no more than a wonky christmas special. A bad one.
